yakut_uruung_aiyy_toyon.name: bestows the kut (life-soul) upon every newborn and grants fertility of people and herds
yakut_uruung_aiyy_toyon.notes: As head of the Aiyy he is the source of the kut, the life-force breathed into infants and livestock; petitioned at Ysyakh for increase of children and foals.

sources.reference: Sieroszewski, Yakuty (The Yakut), 1896
Holmberg (Harva), Finno-Ugric and Siberian Mythology

yakut_uruung_aiyy_toyon.name: emanates pure white light, the supreme expression of his creative power
yakut_uruung_aiyy_toyon.notes: Ürüng (white/bright) names his blinding luminance; in Sakha thought light is life itself.

sources.reference: Holmberg (Harva), Finno-Ugric and Siberian Mythology

yakut_ai_toyon.name: gives the light and warmth of summer, dispelling the long Arctic winter
yakut_ai_toyon.notes: Sakha god of light whose return is celebrated at the midsummer Ysyakh.

sources.reference: Czaplicka, Aboriginal Siberia: A Study in Social Anthropology, 1914

yakut_abaasy.name: moves by a lurching hop-and-drag, being a one-eyed, one-armed, one-legged half-being
yakut_abaasy.notes: Their single-limbed deformity marks them as creatures of imbalance and incompleteness.

sources.reference: Czaplicka, Aboriginal Siberia, 1914

yakut_abaasy.name: bears poisonous blood and iron teeth that contaminate whatever they touch
yakut_abaasy.notes: Iron teeth and venomous blood mark the abaasy as polluting beings of the lower world.

sources.reference: Sieroszewski, Yakuty, 1896

welsh_rhiannon.name: rides a shining white horse at an even pace that no mortal mount can overtake
welsh_rhiannon.notes: In the First Branch her pale steed walks slowly yet outdistances Pwyll's fastest riders until he asks her to stop.

sources.reference: Pwyll Pendefig Dyfed (First Branch of the Mabinogi)

welsh_rhiannon.name: commands the three Birds of Rhiannon, whose song wakes the dead and lulls the living to sleep
welsh_rhiannon.notes: The Adar Rhiannon are named in the Second Branch and in Culhwch ac Olwen as singing far over the sea, waking the dead and lulling the living.

sources.reference: Branwen ferch Llyr (Second Branch); Culhwch ac Olwen

welsh_rhiannon.name: bears the horse-block penance, carrying guests on her back as a mare for a false charge of infanticide
welsh_rhiannon.notes: Wrongly accused of killing her son, she sits at the gate of Arberth offering to carry visitors, an episode echoing her horse-goddess nature.

sources.reference: Pwyll Pendefig Dyfed (First Branch of the Mabinogi)

welsh_gwyn_ap_nudd.name: leads the Wild Hunt, riding with the Cwn Annwn to gather the souls of the dead
welsh_gwyn_ap_nudd.notes: As psychopomp he hunts across the sky with his spectral red-eared hounds; to hear their cry foretold a death.

sources.reference: Rhys, Celtic Folklore: Welsh and Manx, 1901

welsh_gwyn_ap_nudd.name: is set by God to restrain the demons of Annwn lest they destroy the present race
welsh_gwyn_ap_nudd.notes: Culhwch ac Olwen says God placed in him the strength of the demons of Annwfn that the world might not be destroyed.

sources.reference: Culhwch ac Olwen

welsh_gwydion.name: conjures illusory armies, ships and horses to deceive his enemies
welsh_gwydion.notes: He magics phantom fleet and steeds to bargain for Pryderi's swine, the gear vanishing at sundown.

sources.reference: Math fab Mathonwy (Fourth Branch of the Mabinogi)

welsh_gwydion.name: with Math conjures Blodeuwedd, a woman, from the flowers of oak, broom and meadowsweet
welsh_gwydion.notes: To give the cursed Lleu a wife, the two magicians shape a maiden from blossom.

sources.reference: Math fab Mathonwy (Fourth Branch of the Mabinogi)

welsh_gwydion.name: sings the englyn that recalls the wounded eagle Lleu from the oak and restores his human form
welsh_gwydion.notes: By a series of englynion Gwydion lures the dying eagle down branch by branch and strikes him back to a man.

sources.reference: Math fab Mathonwy (Fourth Branch of the Mabinogi)

welsh_blodeuwedd.name: coaxes from Lleu the impossible conditions under which alone he can be slain
welsh_blodeuwedd.notes: Feigning loving concern she learns the only way Lleu can die, betraying it to her lover Gronw.

sources.reference: Math fab Mathonwy (Fourth Branch of the Mabinogi)

welsh_arawn.name: hunts the deer of this world with the red-eared Cwn Annwn
welsh_arawn.notes: Pwyll first meets him following his pale hounds upon a stag in Glyn Cuch.

sources.reference: Pwyll Pendefig Dyfed (First Branch of the Mabinogi)

welsh_math.name: hears whatever the wind carries to him, however softly spoken
welsh_math.notes: The Fourth Branch states that Math heard any word once it reached the wind.

sources.reference: Math fab Mathonwy (Fourth Branch of the Mabinogi)

welsh_math.name: as sovereign judge transforms wrongdoers into mated pairs of beasts for their crimes
welsh_math.notes: He punishes Gwydion and Gilfaethwy by turning them into deer, swine and wolves for three years.

sources.reference: Math fab Mathonwy (Fourth Branch of the Mabinogi)

welsh_amaethon.name: is the only man able to till and dress a certain wild field, set as a task in Culhwch ac Olwen
welsh_amaethon.notes: Ysbaddaden demands Amaethon to plough the land none other can work.

sources.reference: Culhwch ac Olwen

welsh_gofannon.name: forges and sets the iron of Amaethon's plough, work he will do only for a rightful king
welsh_gofannon.notes: One of Ysbaddaden's tasks is to have Gofannon trim the plough-iron at the headland.

sources.reference: Culhwch ac Olwen

welsh_dylan.name: takes on the nature of the sea at once, swimming as well as any fish so that no wave breaks beneath him
welsh_dylan.notes: Named Dylan Eil Ton, son of the wave; on baptism he plunges into the sea.

sources.reference: Math fab Mathonwy (Fourth Branch of the Mabinogi)

welsh_taliesin.name: sings of all ages past and to come, having tasted the three drops of Awen
welsh_taliesin.notes: The Book of Taliesin poems boast knowledge of every age and of his own many transformations and rebirths.

sources.reference: Llyfr Taliesin (Book of Taliesin)
Ystoria Taliesin (Hanes Taliesin)

welsh_taliesin.name: foretells the manner and hour of Maelgwn Gwynedd's death before his court
welsh_taliesin.notes: At Elffin's bidding the boy Taliesin out-sings the king's bards and prophesies the Yellow Plague.

sources.reference: Ystoria Taliesin (Hanes Taliesin)

welsh_pwyll.name: rules Annwn for a year in Arawn's shape and slays Hafgan at the appointed ford
welsh_pwyll.notes: Through the body-exchange he governs the Otherworld justly and defeats Arawn's rival with a single permitted blow, earning the name Pen Annwn.

sources.reference: Pwyll Pendefig Dyfed (First Branch of the Mabinogi)

welsh_pwyll.name: traps the rival suitor Gwawl in a magic bag that can never be filled
welsh_pwyll.notes: Disguised as a beggar on Rhiannon's counsel, he springs the Badger-in-the-Bag game upon Gwawl.

sources.reference: Pwyll Pendefig Dyfed (First Branch of the Mabinogi)

welsh_manawydan.name: snares the enchanter's wife in mouse-form and so forces Llwyd to lift the desolation of Dyfed
welsh_manawydan.notes: He builds a tiny gallows for the pregnant mouse that gnawed his wheat, refusing every ransom until the land and his kin are freed.

sources.reference: Manawydan fab Llyr (Third Branch of the Mabinogi)

welsh_lludd_llaw_eraint.name: rebuilds and walls the chief city of Britain, which is named Caer Lludd after him
welsh_lludd_llaw_eraint.notes: The tale credits him with girding London with walls and towers.

sources.reference: Cyfranc Lludd a Llefelys (Lludd and Llefelys)

welsh_bendigeidfran.name: lays his own giant body across the river Llinon as a bridge for his host
welsh_bendigeidfran.notes: He utters the proverb 'he who would be a leader, let him be a bridge' and spans the unbridgeable Irish river with his body.

sources.reference: Branwen ferch Llyr (Second Branch of the Mabinogi)

welsh_bendigeidfran.name: his severed head keeps living company and prophecy for eighty-seven years before its burial at the White Hill
welsh_bendigeidfran.notes: At his own command the seven survivors bear his uncorrupted, speaking head through the feasting of the Assembly of the Wondrous Head, burying it at last beneath the White Tower of London to ward Britain.

sources.reference: Branwen ferch Llyr (Second Branch of the Mabinogi)

welsh_efnisien.name: breaks the Cauldron of Rebirth from within, shattering it and his own heart to save Britain
welsh_efnisien.notes: Feigning death among the Irish slain he is cast into the cauldron, stretches until it splits in four, and dies.

sources.reference: Branwen ferch Llyr (Second Branch of the Mabinogi)

welsh_caswallawn.name: slays the stewards of Britain unseen beneath a cloak of invisibility and seizes the crown
welsh_caswallawn.notes: Wearing an enchanted mantle he kills six of Caradog's men with a disembodied sword while Bendigeidfran is in Ireland.

sources.reference: Branwen ferch Llyr (Second Branch of the Mabinogi)
Trioedd Ynys Prydein (Welsh Triads)

welsh_branwen.name: rears and teaches a starling to carry word of her bondage across the Irish Sea to her brother
welsh_branwen.notes: Set to drudge in Matholwch's kitchen, she trains a starling and binds her letter to its wing to summon Bendigeidfran.

sources.reference: Branwen ferch Llyr (Second Branch of the Mabinogi)

yakut_uruung_aiyy_toyon.name: Aal Luuk Mas, the cosmic World Tree whose crown rises into his upper world as his hitching-post

sources.reference: Holmberg (Harva), Finno-Ugric and Siberian Mythology

yakut_uruung_aiyy_toyon.name: the serge (ritual hitching-post) raised at Ysyakh, symbol of the World Tree on which the universe rests

sources.reference: Travel Yakutia, Ysyakh festival ethnography

welsh_rhiannon.name: her pale, shining white horse that none can overtake

sources.reference: Pwyll Pendefig Dyfed (First Branch of the Mabinogi)

welsh_gwydion.name: his magic wand (hudlath), with which he transforms shapes and conjures illusions

sources.reference: Math fab Mathonwy (Fourth Branch of the Mabinogi)

welsh_math.name: his magic wand (hudlath), used to test virginity and transform offenders into beasts

sources.reference: Math fab Mathonwy (Fourth Branch of the Mabinogi)

welsh_lludd_llaw_eraint.name: his silver hand, source of the epithet Llaw Eraint

sources.reference: Bromwich, Trioedd Ynys Prydein

welsh_lleu.name: the slate (llech) Lleu sets between himself and Gronw, which Gronw's death-spear pierces in vengeance

sources.reference: Math fab Mathonwy (Fourth Branch of the Mabinogi)

welsh_taliesin.name: his radiant brow, from which Elffin names him Taliesin ('shining brow')

yakut_uruung_aiyy_toyon.name: Ysyakh, the midsummer festival of abundance with libations of kumys to the Aiyy
yakut_uruung_aiyy_toyon.notes: The chief Sakha festival: kumys (fermented mare's milk) is sprinkled toward sky and fire with praises to Aiyy Toyon, with offerings of alaady (pancakes) and salamaat, round-dancing (ohuokai), and a serge hitching-post raised as the World Tree, invoking fertility of people and herds.

sources.reference: Czaplicka, Aboriginal Siberia, 1914
Travel Yakutia / National Geographic, Ysyakh festival ethnography

attributes.name: blinding white radiance and the emblem of the sun
attributes.notes: Personified image of the bright sky enthroned on the ninth heaven.
